items.title: Three suspects detained in Latvia for Tallinn military factory arson
items.summary: Three people have been arrested in Latvia on suspicion of setting fire to the building of the defence industry company ‘Milrem Robotics’ in Tallinn, reports the Estonian public broadcaster ERR.

items.title: Rogue ransomware affiliate poses as recovery firm to steal payments
items.summary: A suspected ransomware affiliate is posing as a ransomware recovery service called "Ransom Busters," contacting the victims before the attacks become public and claiming to be able to provide decryption keys and delete stolen data for a fee. [...]

items.title: Sakura Internet hack exposes data of up to 1.36 million accounts
items.summary: Japanese cloud and data center service provider Sakura Internet disclosed that hackers accessed its sales management system, where customer contract and membership information is stored. [...]

items.summary: Every evening at 21:00, Latvian Radio 1 broadcasts a five-minute summary of the day's news stories in a simplified language format called Ziņas vieglajā valodā ('News in simple language').

items.title: Dissent within Latvian coalition over future airBaltic plan
items.summary: The Greens and Farmers' Union (ZZS) does not agree with its coalition partners over the proposal to give the government the right to invest additional funds in the Latvian national airline airBaltic.

items.title: Renovation of Kuldīga Cultural Centre to resume after 3 year pause
items.summary: Three years ago, the reconstruction of the Kuldīga Cultural Centre was halted by the insolvency of the construction contractor. In order to resume the work, changes were made to the project and new sources of financing were sought. It has now been decided that the renovation will take place in stages, also raising money gradually.

items.title: Electronic health record company CareCloud says 3.7 million people affected by breach
items.summary: Healthcare software firm CareCloud filed documents with the Department of Health and Human Services confirming that 3,756,469 people had information leaked after a hacker spent eight hours in one of the company’s electronic health record environments.

items.title: Hackers compromise 14,500 Dahua web cameras in 35-day campaign
items.summary: In a large-scale campaign that researchers dubbed CameraSwarm, hackers compromised more than 14,500 Dahua IP cameras mostly in Ukraine and Russia. [...]

items.title: NSA, FBI warns of hackers using AI-generated tools in attacks on critical infrastructure technology
items.summary: The National Security Agency (NSA), FBI and other federal agencies said the campaign is targeting Siemens S7 Series PLCs and was being fueled by “AI-assisted development” alongside exploitation of known vulnerabilities.

items.title: US warns of AI-powered attacks on Siemens PLCs in critical infrastructure
items.summary: U.S. cybersecurity agencies warn that threat actors are using AI-generated scripts to exploit Siemens S7 Series programmable logic controllers (PLCs) in U.S. critical infrastructure. [...]

items.title: US charges Iranian hackers over $3.4 billion intellectual property theft
items.summary: The U.S. has charged 17 Iranians, alleged members of a hacking-for-hire company called Mabna Institute, involved in years-long operations that stole data from American organizations. [...]

items.title: 3 suspects detained over suspected arson at Milrem Robotics factory in Estonia
items.summary: Three suspects have been detained in connection with the arson attack on the building of the defense industry company Milrem Robotics, the Prosecutor's Office has said. Initial information suggests the act was premeditated.

items.title: Former Eesti 200 MP joins Parempoolsed
items.summary: Riigikogu member Kalev Stoicescu, who left junior coalition party Eesti 200 last week, said on Wednesday that he had joined the non-parliamentary party, Parempoolsed.

items.title: Estonian raw milk producer to buy Latvia's largest dairy plant
items.summary: Estonia's largest raw milk producer has signed an agreement to acquire Latvia's largest dairy processing company, which, among other things, produces the popular Karūms brand.

items.title: Password spraying attacks surge 155x as hackers exploit MFA gaps
items.summary: Huntress observed a 155x increase in password spraying attacks in H1 2026, including a campaign that generated more than 81 million login attempts in two weeks. The attacks exploited legacy authentication and gaps in MFA policies that left some login flows unprotected. [...]

items.title: Gallery: President of Iceland starts state visit to Estonia
items.summary: The Icelandic head of state, Halla Tómasdóttir, is making a multi-day visit to Estonia this week and will attend the commemorative events marking the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Estonia's independence.

items.title: Estonian firefighters describe intense heat, backburn tactics on Sardinia deployment
items.summary: Sander Etverk, a rescuer from the Tallinn's Nõmme station who helped extinguish forest and landscape fires in Sardinia, said that Italy uses backburning to fight large fires, and two helicopters are constantly in operation, with Estonians also among the crew. The hardest part was coping with the extreme heat, he added.

items.title: Latvian officials resign after cyberattack exposes data on 1.2 million people
items.summary: Latvia’s road traffic agency confirmed that hackers stole data connected to about two-thirds of the country’s population in a major cyberattack that has prompted calls for senior officials to resign.

items.title: Estonian company to buy Latvia's biggest dairy processing business
items.summary: Estonia's Falber Investments OÜ, the parent company of Agrone, Estonia’s largest agricultural group and the region’s largest independent raw milk producer, has signed an agreement to acquire the group of AS Rīgas piena kombināts (RPK), Latvia’s largest dairy processing company, creating a new Baltic dairy behemoth.

items.title: Rare Amur leopard at Tallinn Zoo dies at age 22
items.summary: A rare Amur leopard housed at Tallinn Zoo has died at the age of 22, the zoo announced Tuesday, with staff mourning the loss of one of their most beloved residents.

items.title: Slight increase in hotel stays in second quarter of 2026 in Latvia
items.summary: According to the Central Statistical Bureau data published on August 19, in Q2 2026 the number of non-resident and resident arrivals at Latvian tourist accommodation establishments comprised 750.0 thousand, which is an increase of 1.2 % compared with Q2 2025.

items.title: Kersti Kivirüüt: Multiperspectival history lessons in the service of the nation state
items.summary: Multiperspectival history teaching helps young people distinguish between family memory, propaganda and evidence-based history, providing a stronger foundation for Estonian civic identity, Kersti Kivirüüt writes.

items.title: US charges Iranians for sprawling hacking campaign on government agencies, universities
items.summary: The Justice Department accused 17 alleged hackers with ties to the Iranian government of breaching email accounts at U.S. government agencies and stealing intellectual property from dozens of universities.

items.title: Saaremaa was planted with a Saaremaa‑shaped cornfield
items.summary: Saaremaa island now has its own Saaremaa. A Saaremaa‑shaped maze was created in the Kärla Agricultural Cooperative's cornfield, where fast walkers can tour the entire "island" in just an hour.

items.title: Estonia's ambassador to Ukraine presents credentials to President Zelenskyy
items.summary: Estonia's ambassador to Ukraine, Tiina Intelmann, presented her credentials to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday.

items.title: Vulnerabilities in nnn software
items.summary: CERT Polska has received a report about 4 vulnerabilities (from CVE-2026-65609 to CVE-2026-65612) found in nnn software.

items.title: Former Nõmme Kalju striker Promise David joins Brighton & Hove Albion
items.summary: Promise David, Canada national team striker and former player for Meistriliiga side Nõmme Kalju, has joined Brighton & Hove Albion of the English Premier League (EPL) for the new season.

items.title: Affordable rental flats to be built in Rīga
items.summary: By 2030, it is planned to build 732 affordable rental homes in Rīga – in the Pļavnieki, Ziepniekkalns, and Bolderāja disctricts, according to the agency State Real Estate (Valsts nekustamie īpašumi, VNĪ).

items.title: Critical RCE flaw in Windows IKE Extension now actively exploited
items.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned that hackers are exploiting a critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaw in the Windows Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions component. [...]

items.title: Juhan Kivirähk: How to explain pictures to a (half)dead government?
items.summary: Although politicians in power treat initiatives made outside the Riigikogu chamber dismissively, I believe the next president should take social and economic studies and their use in governing the country under his or her wing and become the patron of creating Estonia's future convention, Juhan Kivirähk writes.

items.title: Latvian police say they have thwarted prison conspiracy
items.summary: The State Police claimed on August 19 that they have foiled a plan organised from within prison to rob and severely beat a man, the police have reported.

items.title: 'Operation Werewolf' sniffs out more illegal border crossers
items.summary: On Tuesday, August 18th, in Krāslava district, soldiers of the National Armed Forces detained someone who was transporting persons who had illegally crossed the state border, according to releases from the State Border Guard and the government.

items.title: TalTech rector concedes presidential race as Ülle Madise emerges as sole candidate
items.summary: Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise is likely the only candidate at the presidential elections, Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) Rector and potential candidate Tiit Land said.

items.title: New tree park to be planted in Latvia as part of World Cleanup Day
items.summary: In one month's time a 10th Happiness Tree Park will be opened as part of the World Cleanup Day, which will take place in approximately 200 countries on September 20th, including Latvia.

items.title: Madise's presidential bid triggers speculation over Estonia's next chancellor of justice
items.summary: The possible election of Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise as president has raised the question of how the role of chancellor of justice will be filled if she assumes the position of head of state.

items.title: Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro reach end of support in 2 months
items.summary: Microsoft has reminded customers that systems running Home and Pro editions of Windows 11 24H2 will stop receiving updates in two months. [...]

items.title: Bears entering yards in Ida‑Viru County tranquilized and returned to forest
items.summary: Two young bears were captured with a tranquilizer rifle in Ida‑Viru County after once again entering people's yards. The bears, which the Environmental Board had earlier moved from Tartu County to Ida‑Viru County in hopes they would stop disturbing residents, were returned to the forest.

items.title: Latvian CSDD bosses step down
items.summary: All board members of the Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) have submitted a letter to the Minister for Transport, Rihards Kozlovskis (New Unity), Kozlovskis said on Wednesday, August 19.

items.title: CISA: Medusa ransomware hit over 500 critical infrastructure orgs
items.summary: The FBI said Tuesday that the Medusa ransomware gang has breached more than 500 critical infrastructure organizations in the United States since June 2021. [...]

items.title: Latvian and Lithuanian national militias stand shoulder to shoulder
items.summary: Celebrating the 35th anniversary of the National Guard (Zemessardze), the National Guard has signed a memorandum of cooperation with the Lithuanian Riflemen's Union (Lietuvos šaulių sąjunga) to strengthen cooperation and exchange of experience between the two organizations.

items.title: Holdout MP declines to endorse justice chancellor as presidential candidate
items.summary: A Riigikogu member who had held out on signing for Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise's presidential bid now says she will not endorse Madise or any other candidate.

items.title: Presidential candidate Ülle Madise: Estonia must look to its own interests
items.summary: Estonia must look after its own interests and do what benefits the country while remaining a valuable partner to its allies, presidential candidate Ülle Madise tells ERR in an interview.

items.title: Latvian citizen to be prosecuted for war glorification
items.summary: On 14 August this year, the State Security Service (VDD) urged the Public Prosecutor’s Office to initiate criminal proceedings against a Latvian citizen for the prolonged and systematic glorification and justification of the war waged by Russia in Ukraine, inciting hatred against Ukrainians, as well as the unauthorised possession of a high-powered air gun and explosives.

items.title: New rules will let Latvian army requisition private land in an emergency
items.summary: On Tuesday, August 18th, the Cabinet of Ministers supported amendments to the National Security Law proposed by the Ministry of Defence, which provide for granting the National Armed Forces the temporary right to use land owned by private individuals, if it is deemed necessary for national defence.

items.title: Forest report warns Estonia is cutting trees faster than they can regrow
items.summary: A forest inventory published by the Estonian Environment Agency shows that Estonia's forests are not recovering fast enough. The sector also lacks consensus on how much forest should be protected and how much should be harvested.

items.title: CSDD boss ready to quit over massive database leak
items.summary: The head of the Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD), Aivars Aksenoks, is preparing to resign from his position after the investigation into the cyberattack that the CSDD experienced in early August is completed, Aksenoks announced in an interview with Latvian Television's "Morning Panorama" on August 19th.

items.title: 'Psychics' scam two women for over 150 thousand euros in Latvia
items.summary: Two women, having fallen for advertisements posted on the social networking site ‘Facebook’ which purported to offer the services of psychics, transferred a total of more than 150,000 euros to the fraudsters, the State Police reported on August 18.

items.title: Madise becomes clear front‑runner after Isamaa endorsement
items.summary: Isamaa's support for Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise in the presidential election means she has become the clear front‑runner. Even if some votes slip away in the secret ballot, four parties together have enough votes to elect the president in the Riigikogu's first round on September 2.

items.title: Some rain across most of Latvia Wednesday
items.summary: Forecasts indicate that brief showers are expected in many parts of Latvia on Wednesday.

items.title: Ban on credit advertising lifted in Latvia
items.summary: From Wednesday, 18 August, the ban on consumer credit advertising has been lifted, whilst strict requirements have been imposed on the content of such adverts, Latvian Radio reported on August 19.

items.title: Sunny summer means strong cucumber harvest for Estonia
items.summary: A sunny summer has brought Estonia's cucumber growers a strong harvest, with more than a million domestic cucumbers destined for preserves production this season.

items.title: Estonian agency refuses to share fallen Ukrainian soldier's health data with his children
items.summary: The Tallinn Administrative Court found that minor children have the right to access the dental records of their father, who has been declared dead, if the records are needed to identify what may be his remains in Ukraine.

items.title: Tallinn criticizes organization of the state's planned Ukraine recovery conference
items.summary: The Tallinn City Government has criticized the organization of an international conference on aid to Ukraine set to take place next January, including concerns that participants may have to trudge through snowdrifts.

items.title: Latvian government weakens protection for larger trees
items.summary: The Latvian government decided on Tuesday, August 18, that larger trees will be allowed to be cut down outside forests than were previously allowed to be felled.

items.title: News in simple Latvian: 18th August, 2026
items.summary: Every evening at 21:00, Latvian Radio 1 broadcasts a five-minute summary of the day's news stories in a simplified language format called Ziņas vieglajā valodā ('News in simple language').

items.title: More than 200 victims of Medusa ransomware identified over the last year, CISA says
items.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and FBI updated an advisory on the group initially released in March 2025 — writing that as of April 2026, Medusa actors have hit more than 500 victims. CISA previously said 300 victims, many of which are in critical infrastructure sectors, were attacked as of 2025.

items.title: Clop created custom web shell for Windchill data theft attacks
items.summary: A custom Java web shell likely linked to the Clop ransomware gang was designed specifically for PTC Windchill and FlexPLM servers, with built-in features to decrypt credentials, enumerate file repositories, and steal files. [...]

items.title: Pesticide residues in agricultural soils on the rise
items.summary: Pesticide residues in Estonia's arable soils are going up, the state Environment Agency (Keskkonnaagentuur) says.

items.title: Erkki Keldo: Idealizing others' success overshadows Estonia's economic growth
items.summary: The economy does not grow if we ourselves consistently pound our business environment into the mud and proclaim to the world that there is no point in investing in Estonia, writes Erkki Keldo.

items.title: Isamaa backs Ülle Madise in presidential election
items.summary: Isamaa will support Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise's candidacy in the presidential election, party chair Urmas Reinsalu said. Just a few hours earlier, it became clear that the Estonian Center Party will support Tiit Land's candidacy.

items.title: Your Controls Block Known Attacks. What About the Behavior?
items.summary: Security controls can block a familiar attack method while missing quieter ways to achieve the same objective. Picus Security's Blue Report 2026 shows how prevention rates can vary dramatically by technique and why behavioral testing is needed to uncover those gaps. [...]

items.title: Karoliina Ainge: How big is Estonia after its next president?
items.summary: When discussing the president's foreign‑policy role, we often use the phrase "introducing Estonia to the world." In the 1990s, that was an understandable goal, but for today's Estonia it is far too modest. The Estonian president now has something much more valuable at their disposal: the diplomatic capital accumulated over decades, writes Karoliina Ainge.

items.title: Ukrainians plan to sing Latvian national anthem in Rīga
items.summary: At midday on August 22nd, at at the Freedom Monument in Rīga, the Latvian anthem will ring out, but this time it will not be sung by Latvians.

items.title: Gallery: Former Estonian PMs meet for annual pre-August 20 lunch
items.summary: Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) hosted his predecessors in Tallinn Tuesday for the 10th annual Estonian prime ministers' lunch ahead of Restoration of Independence Day.

items.title: EDF to combine medical services under new battalion command
items.summary: The Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) is to centralize its medical services into one battalion, with the project due for completion by year-end.

items.title: Data of 1.2 million people breached in recent CSDD cyberattack
items.summary: The Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) reported on August 18 that personal data relating to 1.2 million people was obtained in a cyberattack. Latvia's total population is a little over 1.8 million, so as a proportion of the population, the breach is enormous.

items.title: Latvian State Police wants to put lawyer in the dock
items.summary: The Latvian State Police has completed an investigation into the actions of sworn attorney Inese Šulte and another private individual, requesting that both be charged with attemtping to influence a suspect, the LETA newswire reports.

items.title: Report: Fifth of platform taxi drivers and food couriers in a career dead end
items.summary: One in five people providing ride-hailing or courier services through digital platforms is stuck in a career dead end, working full time in a field for which they consider themselves overqualified, a new report finds.

items.title: Estonian defense contractor Milrem Robotics' fire could have been arson
items.summary: A building used by Milrem Robotics on Betooni tänav in Tallinn burned overnight into Saturday. Investigators are examining possible motives, including a potential act of sabotage.

items.title: Tallinn deputy mayor: 854 youths without study place 2 weeks before new school year
items.summary: Tallinn still has 854 young people left without a study place, nearly a fifth of basic school graduates, Deputy Mayor Andrei Kante said, calling the situation critical.

items.title: Special Saeima sitting will mark 35th restoration of 'de facto' independence
items.summary: On August 21st – the day when Latvia's independence was de facto restored 35 years ago – the Saeima will gather for a special ceremonial sitting at 12:00.

items.title: Ex-Reform MP: No one's collecting signatures for Land's presidential bid
items.summary: MP Meelis Kiili says there is no organized push to gather signatures to nominate TalTech rector Tiit Land for president, despite efforts to rally support among independents.

items.title: Center Party backs Tiit Land for Estonia's presidency
items.summary: At the joint meeting of the Center Party's board and its Riigikogu faction, it was decided to support the candidacy of Tallinn University of Technology rector Tiit Land in the presidential election.

items.title: Revoking Swedish prison rental scheme just requires political will
items.summary: The prison rental agreement between Estonia and Sweden could be terminated relatively easily if there were the political will to do so, said Rait Kuuse, head of the Estonian Prison Service.

items.title: Only in Latvia: new train named after particularly popular mushroom
items.summary: The Latvian mania for funghi is well documented, and on August 18th gets another entry with news that a shiny new passenger train will be honoured with the name of a particularly popular species of edible mushroom.

items.title: Apartment prices differ 51 times in Estonia's most expensive and cheapest cities
items.summary: The gap in apartment prices per square meter between Tallinn and lower-income areas has grown to as much as 51-fold. Estonia's cheapest apartments are located in Ida-Viru County, Delfi reports.

items.title: Expert: Russia's war‑driven economic boom is running out of steam
items.summary: Russia's early wartime economic surge, fueled by defense production and massive state spending, is showing clear signs of exhaustion, Bank of Estonia economist Peeter Luikmel says.

items.title: Photos: First Swedish prisoners arrive at Tartu under prison‑rental deal
items.summary: On Tuesday, the first four Swedish inmates arrived at Tartu Prison under the prison‑rental agreement concluded between Estonia and Sweden.

items.title: Latvia spends less than EU average on education
items.summary: New data published by Eurostat shows levels of public spending on education across the European Union – and reveals that Latvia spends less than the majority of its EU peers on this crucial investment in the future.

items.title: Climate physicist: El Niño to bring higher food prices to Estonia
items.summary: The exceptionally strong climate-altering El Niño pattern this year is likely to affect Estonia through rising food prices from the latter part of this year, according to one expert.

items.title: Vulnerability in Carbone software
items.summary: Improper handling of highly compressed data (data amplification) vulnerability (CVE-2026-18929) has been found in Carbone software.

items.title: Holdout Reform MP backs justice chancellor presidential bid, signatures reach 63
items.summary: A Reform Party MP initially hesitant on backing Justice Chancellor Ülle Madise as a candidate at next month's presidential election now says he supports her.

items.title: Tartu mulls keeping bike-sharing program
items.summary: Despite plans revealed this spring to end Tartu's bike-sharing program, the city intends to keep it running while seeking ways to cut costs. Meanwhile, Bolt will soon launch a conventional bike rental service in Tartu.

items.title: Estonia's war museums: Small sites struggle, national museum thriving
items.summary: With the number of foreign occupiers of Estonia through history, it is no surprise that the country is home to a variety of museums displaying militaria.

items.title: EU packaging rule change prompts confusion, online shops halt foreign orders
items.summary: Since last Wednesday, a new packaging and packaging‑waste regulation has been in force in the European Union. One of the changes requires businesses to register in the producer register of every member state where they sell goods.

items.title: More sauce? Spilva expands its Babīte factory
items.summary: Food manufacturer “Orkla Latvija” plans to invest 5.4 million euros in the modernisation of the “Spilva” sauce and ready-meal production facility in Babīte, the company said on August 18.

items.title: Four migrants caught in Ķekava municipality, Latvia
items.summary: On Tuesday morning, August 18, the Ķekava Municipal Police detained four migrants on the Rīga bypass between the Daugmale roundabout and the Riga Hydroelectric Power Station and handed them over to the State Border Guard, the municipal police said.

items.title: Delfi poll: Nearly a third back Ülle Madise as next president
items.summary: Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise was the people's pick for president by nearly a third of respondents to a survey, Delfi reported.

items.title: Estonian traders not daunted by ban on destroying unsold clothing
items.summary: A ban on selling unsold clothing and footwear will have little impact on Estonian retailers and manufacturers, as discounts generally help them sell nearly all their products.

items.title: Public invited to choose their Latvian building of the year
items.summary: The organizers of the Best Building of the Year in Latvia 2025 competition – the Latvian Builders' Association and the Latvian Union of Civil Engineers – are inviting the public to vote for the buildings submitted for the competition and put into operation in 2025, which are of the most benefit to society.

items.title: Vidzeme farmers happy with this year's grain harvest
items.summary: Combine harvesters are active in the grain fields of Vidzeme right now as they seek to get their grain into storage during dry conditions. Farmers assess this year as successful in terms of harvest, despite increases in the price of mineral fertilizers and fuel, and some rains early in the season.

items.title: Elron resumes Tallinn–Narva rail service on eastbound route
items.summary: Elron's eastbound passenger rail service resumed early Tuesday afternoon after a damaged overhead line halted trains on the Tallinn–Narva route for several hours.

items.title: 'Buckle up' signal to sound throughout Latvia on Tuesday
items.summary: On Tuesday, 18 August, at 11:00, a signal warning of a seatbelt not being fastened will be broadcast on radio stations and at petrol stations. This will mark the start of the Road Traffic Safety Directorate’s (CSDD) new campaign: “The last dance begins without a seatbelt. Don’t take chances – buckle up!”, CSDD said in a release.

items.title: Rinkēvičs: Latvia lacks border guards
items.summary: Significant progress has been made in the construction of infrastructure along the Latvian–Belarusian border, but there are serious problems with human resources – this was the conclusion reached by President Edgars Rinkēvičs during a visit to Piedruja, a village on the border with Belarus, on August 18.

items.title: News in simple Latvian: 17th August, 2026
items.summary: Every evening at 21:00, Latvian Radio 1 broadcasts a five-minute summary of the day's news stories in a simplified language format called Ziņas vieglajā valodā ('News in simple language').

items.title: airBaltic bondholders agree to capitalise interest payments
items.summary: Bondholders of the national airline ‘airBaltic’ voted in favour of capitalising interest payments on the bonds at a meeting on Monday, 17 August, the airline announced.

items.title: State Security Service demands prosecution of Daugavpils separatist
items.summary: On August 17th, the Latvian State Security Service (VDD) said that a week earlier it had asked the Prosecution Office to initiate criminal prosecution against a Latvian 'non-citizen' for expressing support towards ideas directed against the territorial integrity of Latvia.

items.title: President Rinkēvičs returns to Latvia's eastern border
items.summary: On August 17th Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs made another one of his regular visits to the country's eastern border.

items.title: Diver lost in Baltic sea in July found
items.summary: The body of a diver who went missing in mid-July has been found in the sea off Roja, the State Police (VP) reported on Monday, 17 August.

items.title: Latvian central bank's 'Financial Stability Report' available in English
items.summary: The Latvian central bank, Latvijas Banka (LB) has published its annual Financial Stability Report in English. A report has been published every year since 2003 "to raise public awareness regarding the development of the Latvian financial system and to draw attention to systemic risks."

items.title: Finance Minister, central bank governor talk future EU funds
items.summary: At the end of last week, Finance Minister Māris Kučinskis (United List) met with Bank of Latvia (LB) Governor Mārtiņš Kazāks to discuss possible cooperation between the Ministry of Finance (FM) and the LB in preparation for the next European Union (EU) funds planning period 2028-2034.

items.title: Company registration numbers down in Latvia, but so are bankruptcies
items.summary: In the second quarter of 2026, registrations of businesses in the EU decreased by 0.5% compared with the first quarter of 2026, while bankruptcies increased by 5.7% according to data on business registrations and bankruptcies published by Eurostat today.

items.title: Latvians spent EUR 619 monthly on household needs last year
items.summary: In 2025, mean monthly household consumption expenditure per household member amounted to 619 euros, according to Central Statistical Bureau data published on August 17.

items.title: Vulnerability in OutSystems Service Center software
items.summary: DOM-based Cross-site Scripting vulnerability (CVE-2026-40126) has been found in OutSystems Service Center software.

items.title: Scammer e-mails 'from Swedbank' active again in Latvia
items.summary: On Monday, August 17, Swedbank customers have again received targeted emails from scammers, Swedbank said in a statement.

items.title: Ülle Madise meets with MPs to discuss presidential candidacy
items.summary: Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, who announced that she has agreed to run for president, met with the Riigikogu parliamentary groups on Monday and Tuesday to discuss her candidacy with MPs.

items.title: Drone that was shot down in Latvia entered from Belarus
items.summary: The drone shot down in the Balvi region on Friday flew into Latvian airspace from Belarus, Defence Minister Raivis Melnis said in an interview on Latvian Television on Monday morning.

items.title: 'Last chance' to save airBaltic, says Latvian Prime Minister
